subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas uniform viewport fitting

criteria.rationale: fitScale returns one factor, Math.min(availW/canvas.width, availH/canvas.height), clamped below by MIN_SCALE. Stage applies it as transform: scale(scale) on the fixed-size canvas, so the composition scales uniformly without reflow. subcomponents.title: Detects a missing reference sample

criteria.rationale: The review guidance says a missing sample includes a reference sample whose outline or steps content (titles, captions, steps) is absent. It also says such a failure must show up as a non-zero exit at a check that names the build or sample phase, not as a later browser or render timeout. Here is what the verifier does, in order. main() (scripts/verify.mjs:83-117) runs build(), then readRegistry, then validateRegistry. That is the only check before the browser starts. validateRegistry (scripts/lib/checks.mjs:23-30) works on the registry entries that parseRegistry pulls out of src/presentations/index.ts with a regex (scripts/lib/registry.mjs:4-20). Those entries carry only slug, title and loader. So it checks three things: the slug is registered, the title matches, and the loader file exists. It never reads the sample's steps, titles or captions. main() then prints 'ok sample' and moves straight to withPreview and renderSteps (verify.mjs:93-110). There is no other step-content check before rendering. The sample's steps come from STEPS in steps/index.ts (lines 6-27). Talk.tsx (lines 1-14) passes STEPS to Presentation as `steps`. If those steps are absent, for example an empty array, Presentation (Presentation.tsx:39-42) finds steps[nav.index] undefined and returns null, so the data-step-count hook (line 52) never renders. renderSteps (verify.mjs:41-50) then waits 10000ms for '[data-step-count]' and throws VerifyError('render', '... did not render the step-count hook'). That throw comes before validateStepCount (line 57) and validateSampleStep (line 70), the only places outline titles, captions and step count are compared. The failure is therefore a render-phase timeout, and it is reported as 'FAIL render' rather than as a sample or outline mismatch. That is exactly the case the guidance excludes. Judges A and C credit validateRegistry and the e2e faults for an unregistered slug and for out-of-order steps. Those faults do fail with a sample-phase message. But both reorder cases still render steps and reach validateSampleStep. Neither judge's material addresses the guidance's explicit absent-steps-content case, which takes the render-timeout path above. So their reasons do not show the whole requirement is met. Judge B's reason matches the cited source and decides the requirement.

criteria.rationale: All nine public primitives (Node, Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Arrow, Appear, SceneLayer) meet all three clauses. (1) Typed props: NodeProps extends GeometryProps and Omit<HTMLMotionProps<'div'>, 'id'|'layoutId'|'children'>. Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip use or extend NodeProps. ArrowProps extends Omit<SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>, ...>. Appear takes Omit<HTMLMotionProps<'div'>, 'initial'|'animate'>. SceneLayer takes HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>. None uses Record<string, unknown>. Arrow spreads `rest as object` onto motion.svg. That cast only works around the motion/SVG type mismatch, and rest is still the typed SVG-props remainder. (2) Identity hooks come after caller props: Node spreads {...rest} first, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-entity and data-presentation-node={kind}. Arrow spreads rest, then sets data-presentation-entity and data-presentation-node='arrow'. Appear spreads props, then sets data-presentation-appear. SceneLayer spreads props, then sets data-presentation-scene-layer. Frame, Emphasis and Label are thin wrappers, <Node kind='...' {...props} />. NodeProps has no kind field, so a typed caller cannot override it, and Node writes the hooks last anyway. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM: Node destructures kind, id, x, y, width, height, style, children and appear. Box and SymbolChip destructure Icon and symbol. Arrow destructures id, from, to, bend, bidirectional, style and appear. None of these reaches the spread. The bootstrap template copies have the same spread-then-hook ordering, per a grep of that nodes directory.

votes.rationale: Grouping: all nine steps come from one META.map in steps/index.ts, with the same Scene (SampleScene) and groupKey 'sample'. Stage keys its motion.div with sceneKey(step). sceneKey returns `group:${groupKey}:${sceneId}` when groupKey is set, and the id is looked up per Scene component. All nine steps therefore get the same key, one scene instance stays mounted, and only payload.n changes. Identity: this is separate from groupKey. ENTITIES in entities.ts holds the presentation-owned ids. SampleScene renders every entity with key={e.id} and passes id={e.id} (or id from Card) to Box, Label, Frame or SymbolChip. Those components go through Node, which sets layoutId={id} on a motion.div inside Stage's LayoutGroup. An entity present in consecutive steps keeps its id and persists or morphs. Edges use EDGES ids, passed as Arrow id and data-presentation-entity. Arrow has no layoutId. It keeps a path-continuity map keyed by that id, and it stays mounted under the grouped scene.

votes.rationale: The code is split along clear lines. Presentation-specific code is in src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/: entities.ts (ids and geometry), steps/index.ts (step metadata), steps/scene.tsx (scene rendering), Talk.tsx (wiring) and talk.css (look). The reusable kit is in src/presentation-kit/ and has no demo knowledge. The registry in src/presentations/index.ts is a one-line-per-talk list that lazy-loads Talk. Public inputs I traced are used: the Talk's `title` is passed to Presentation, which puts it on the root as data-presentation-title-text, so the contract is consumed and not ignored. `initialMode` goes to usePresentationNav, and `className` goes to the root. EDGES and ENTITIES are each consumed by SampleScene. `entity()` is used by Card. The ATTRIBUTION constant is consumed in Presentation, and CHROME and STAGE_LAYOUT are consumed by chrome and Stage. I found no dead constants or duplicated mechanisms.

result.rationale: The review guidance says a missing sample includes a reference sample whose outline or steps content (titles, captions, steps) is absent. It also says such a failure must show up as a non-zero exit at a check that names the build or sample phase, not as a later browser or render timeout. Here is what the verifier does, in order. main() (scripts/verify.mjs:83-117) runs build(), then readRegistry, then validateRegistry. That is the only check before the browser starts. validateRegistry (scripts/lib/checks.mjs:23-30) works on the registry entries that parseRegistry pulls out of src/presentations/index.ts with a regex (scripts/lib/registry.mjs:4-20). Those entries carry only slug, title and loader. So it checks three things: the slug is registered, the title matches, and the loader file exists. It never reads the sample's steps, titles or captions. main() then prints 'ok sample' and moves straight to withPreview and renderSteps (verify.mjs:93-110). There is no other step-content check before rendering. The sample's steps come from STEPS in steps/index.ts (lines 6-27). Talk.tsx (lines 1-14) passes STEPS to Presentation as `steps`. If those steps are absent, for example an empty array, Presentation (Presentation.tsx:39-42) finds steps[nav.index] undefined and returns null, so the data-step-count hook (line 52) never renders. renderSteps (verify.mjs:41-50) then waits 10000ms for '[data-step-count]' and throws VerifyError('render', '... did not render the step-count hook'). That throw comes before validateStepCount (line 57) and validateSampleStep (line 70), the only places outline titles, captions and step count are compared. The failure is therefore a render-phase timeout, and it is reported as 'FAIL render' rather than as a sample or outline mismatch. That is exactly the case the guidance excludes. Judges A and C credit validateRegistry and the e2e faults for an unregistered slug and for out-of-order steps. Those faults do fail with a sample-phase message. But both reorder cases still render steps and reach validateSampleStep. Neither judge's material addresses the guidance's explicit absent-steps-content case, which takes the render-timeout path above. So their reasons do not show the whole requirement is met. Judge B's reason matches the cited source and decides the requirement.

verification-tooling.rationale: The review guidance says a missing sample includes a reference sample whose outline or steps content (titles, captions, steps) is absent. It also says such a failure must show up as a non-zero exit at a check that names the build or sample phase, not as a later browser or render timeout. Here is what the verifier does, in order. main() (scripts/verify.mjs:83-117) runs build(), then readRegistry, then validateRegistry. That is the only check before the browser starts. validateRegistry (scripts/lib/checks.mjs:23-30) works on the registry entries that parseRegistry pulls out of src/presentations/index.ts with a regex (scripts/lib/registry.mjs:4-20). Those entries carry only slug, title and loader. So it checks three things: the slug is registered, the title matches, and the loader file exists. It never reads the sample's steps, titles or captions. main() then prints 'ok sample' and moves straight to withPreview and renderSteps (verify.mjs:93-110). There is no other step-content check before rendering. The sample's steps come from STEPS in steps/index.ts (lines 6-27). Talk.tsx (lines 1-14) passes STEPS to Presentation as `steps`. If those steps are absent, for example an empty array, Presentation (Presentation.tsx:39-42) finds steps[nav.index] undefined and returns null, so the data-step-count hook (line 52) never renders. renderSteps (verify.mjs:41-50) then waits 10000ms for '[data-step-count]' and throws VerifyError('render', '... did not render the step-count hook'). That throw comes before validateStepCount (line 57) and validateSampleStep (line 70), the only places outline titles, captions and step count are compared. The failure is therefore a render-phase timeout, and it is reported as 'FAIL render' rather than as a sample or outline mismatch. That is exactly the case the guidance excludes. Judges A and C credit validateRegistry and the e2e faults for an unregistered slug and for out-of-order steps. Those faults do fail with a sample-phase message. But both reorder cases still render steps and reach validateSampleStep. Neither judge's material addresses the guidance's explicit absent-steps-content case, which takes the render-timeout path above. So their reasons do not show the whole requirement is met. Judge B's reason matches the cited source and decides the requirement.

votes.rationale: Readiness comes from HTTP polling of the port, not from the child's own announcement. votes.rationale: All nine public primitives (Node, Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Arrow, Appear, SceneLayer) meet all three clauses. (1) Typed props: NodeProps extends GeometryProps and Omit<HTMLMotionProps<'div'>, 'id'|'layoutId'|'children'>. Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip use or extend NodeProps. ArrowProps extends Omit<SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>, ...>. Appear takes Omit<HTMLMotionProps<'div'>, 'initial'|'animate'>. SceneLayer takes HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>. None uses Record<string, unknown>. Arrow spreads `rest as object` onto motion.svg. That cast only works around the motion/SVG type mismatch, and rest is still the typed SVG-props remainder. (2) Identity hooks come after caller props: Node spreads {...rest} first, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-entity and data-presentation-node={kind}. Arrow spreads rest, then sets data-presentation-entity and data-presentation-node='arrow'. Appear spreads props, then sets data-presentation-appear. SceneLayer spreads props, then sets data-presentation-scene-layer. Frame, Emphasis and Label are thin wrappers, <Node kind='...' {...props} />. NodeProps has no kind field, so a typed caller cannot override it, and Node writes the hooks last anyway. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM: Node destructures kind, id, x, y, width, height, style, children and appear. Box and SymbolChip destructure Icon and symbol. Arrow destructures id, from, to, bend, bidirectional, style and appear. None of these reaches the spread. The bootstrap template copies have the same spread-then-hook ordering, per a grep of that nodes directory.

scene-kit.rationale: The source meets the requirement. Continuing entities use LAYOUT_T (duration 0.5, delay 0). In Node this is the `transition` prop for layout, and in Arrow it is the path-morph transition. Newcomers get `initial: {opacity: 0}` and `animate: ENTER_ANIMATE`. ENTER_ANIMATE's transition delay is ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T.delay + LAYOUT_T.duration = 0.5. That is at least the layout duration, so the visible entry starts no earlier than the persisting layout motion ends. The delay sits only in the opacity entry transition, and only when `appear` is true. Continuing entities get no delay on their layout motion. In scene.tsx every identified entity goes through a kit primitive that forwards `appear`. `EntityView` spreads `g`, which includes `appear`, into Box, Label, SymbolChip or Frame in every case. This covers the default morph-label branch, and Card passes `appear` to Box. Every Arrow edge gets `appear={entering(e.since)}`. `entering` is `since > previous`, and `usePrevious` keeps `previous` stable while the step is shown. So `appear` is true only for entities introduced on the current transition. No sample entity is rendered through plain markup without entry motion. The unit tests agree: the persisting layout transition equals LAYOUT_T, the newcomer's delay is at least layout.delay + layout.duration, and the sample's newly introduced step cards have initial opacity 0 and the delayed animate.

verification-tooling.rationale: Readiness comes from HTTP polling via probe(url). None of these reaches a DOM spread. The bootstrap template copies of Node.tsx and Arrow.tsx are identical to the repository versions. geometry.ts is not in the packet, but Node passes exactly x, y, width and height to geometryStyle, which indicates that is the whole GeometryProps surface.

votes.rationale: Readiness comes from HTTP polling of the port, not from the child's own announcement. The only ownership check is the child's exit state, sampled by failed() at the top of each poll loop iteration, and it is not raced against the probe. If another process took the freshly picked port between pickFreePort closing it and the preview starting, a 200 from that server could be accepted before the child's strictPort failure was observed. The ephemeral port and --strictPort alone are insufficient under the review guidance.

pickFreePort closes the server before the child binds, leaving a window where another server can answer the probe.

ArrowProps extends Omit<SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>, ...>. Appear takes Omit<HTMLMotionProps<'div'>, 'initial'|'animate'>. SceneLayer takes HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>. Arrow spreads rest, then sets data-presentation-entity and data-presentation-node='arrow'. Appear spreads props, then sets data-presentation-appear. SceneLayer spreads props, then sets data-presentation-scene-layer. Frame, Emphasis and Label are thin wrappers, <Node kind='...' {...props} />. NodeProps has no kind field, so a typed caller cannot override it, and Node writes the hooks last anyway. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM: Node destructures kind, id, x, y, width, height, style, children and appear. Box and SymbolChip destructure Icon and symbol. Arrow destructures id, from, to, bend, bidirectional, style and appear. None of these reaches the spread. The bootstrap template copies have the same spread-then-hook ordering, per a grep of that nodes directory.

It also says such a failure must show up as a non-zero exit at a check that names the build or sample phase, not as a later browser or render timeout. Here is what the verifier does, in order. main() (scripts/verify.mjs:83-117) runs build(), then readRegistry, then validateRegistry. That is the only check before the browser starts. validateRegistry (scripts/lib/checks.mjs:23-30) works on the registry entries that parseRegistry pulls out of src/presentations/index.ts with a regex (scripts/lib/registry.mjs:4-20). Those entries carry only slug, title and loader. So it checks three things: the slug is registered, the title matches, and the loader file exists. It never reads the sample's steps, titles or captions. main() then prints 'ok sample' and moves straight to withPreview and renderSteps (verify.mjs:93-110). There is no other step-content check before rendering. The sample's steps come from STEPS in steps/index.ts (lines 6-27). Talk.tsx (lines 1-14) passes STEPS to Presentation as `steps`. If those steps are absent, for example an empty array, Presentation (Presentation.tsx:39-42) finds steps[nav.index] undefined and returns null, so the data-step-count hook (line 52) never renders. renderSteps (verify.mjs:41-50) then waits 10000ms for '[data-step-count]' and throws VerifyError('render', '... did not render the step-count hook'). That throw comes before validateStepCount (line 57) and validateSampleStep (line 70), the only places outline titles, captions and step count are compared. The failure is therefore a render-phase timeout, and it is reported as 'FAIL render' rather than as a sample or outline mismatch. That is exactly the case the guidance excludes. Judges A and C credit validateRegistry and the e2e faults for an unregistered slug and for out-of-order steps. Those faults do fail with a sample-phase message. But both reorder cases still render steps and reach validateSampleStep. Neither judge's material addresses the guidance's explicit absent-steps-content case, which takes the render-timeout path above. So their reasons do not show the whole requirement is met. Judge B's reason matches the cited source and decides the requirement.

result.rationale: The review guidance says a missing sample includes a reference sample whose outline or steps content (titles, captions, steps) is absent. It also says such a failure must show up as a non-zero exit at a check that names the build or sample phase, not as a later browser or render timeout. Here is what the verifier does, in order. main() (scripts/verify.mjs:83-117) runs build(), then readRegistry, then validateRegistry. That is the only check before the browser starts. validateRegistry (scripts/lib/checks.mjs:23-30) works on the registry entries that parseRegistry pulls out of src/presentations/index.ts with a regex (scripts/lib/registry.mjs:4-20). Those entries carry only slug, title and loader. So it checks three things: the slug is registered, the title matches, and the loader file exists. It never reads the sample's steps, titles or captions. main() then prints 'ok sample' and moves straight to withPreview and renderSteps (verify.mjs:93-110). There is no other step-content check before rendering. The sample's steps come from STEPS in steps/index.ts (lines 6-27). Talk.tsx (lines 1-14) passes STEPS to Presentation as `steps`. If those steps are absent, for example an empty array, Presentation (Presentation.tsx:39-42) finds steps[nav.index] undefined and returns null, so the data-step-count hook (line 52) never renders. renderSteps (verify.mjs:41-50) then waits 10000ms for '[data-step-count]' and throws VerifyError('render', '... did not render the step-count hook'). That throw comes before validateStepCount (line 57) and validateSampleStep (line 70), the only places outline titles, captions and step count are compared. The failure is therefore a render-phase timeout, and it is reported as 'FAIL render' rather than as a sample or outline mismatch. That is exactly the case the guidance excludes. Judges A and C credit validateRegistry and the e2e faults for an unregistered slug and for out-of-order steps. Those faults do fail with a sample-phase message. But both reorder cases still render steps and reach validateSampleStep. Neither judge's material addresses the guidance's explicit absent-steps-content case, which takes the render-timeout path above. So their reasons do not show the whole requirement is met. Judge B's reason matches the cited source and decides the requirement.

Each starts the verify or inspect script through run(), which is a blocking spawnSync (tests/helpers/project-copy.ts:34-37). Each asserts only after that process has exited, on its status, stdout/stderr, screenshot files and leak/port state. None contains a fixed sleep, a waitForTimeout, or a count read used as a wait. The setTimeout at verify.e2e.test.ts:63 is text injected into the app source, not a test wait. The settle-timing test (inspect.int.test.ts:62-68) compares file mtimes after the spawned run has finished. The unit tests are barred from Playwright and browser launch (repo-contract.test.ts:35-40). So the 200ms sleep in project-copy.test.ts:15 waits on a plain node child, not a browser test, and the waitForTimeout in inspect-checks.test.ts:135 belongs to a fake page. The fixed settle delays come only after that check. The review guidance says longer fixed settle delays earn no credit and cause no fail. Judge C's dissent therefore does not show a clause of the requirement unmet.

result.rationale: Only three delivered test files cause a browser to run: tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts, tests/integration/inspect.int.test.ts and tests/integration/bootstrap.int.test.ts. Each one runs the project's verify or inspect script through `run()`, which is a blocking `spawnSync` in tests/helpers/project-copy.ts:34-37. Each then asserts on the finished process's exit status, stdout/stderr, screenshot files and leak/port state. None of these tests drives a Playwright page itself. The three files, quoted in full, contain no fixed sleep, waitForTimeout or count-read used as a wait. The `setTimeout` at verify.e2e.test.ts:63 is fault-injection code written into the app's source, not a test wait. Within the scripts these tests run, every step transition is awaited by the polling `waitForIndex` (scripts/lib/checks.mjs:54-68). It polls `data-step-index` every 50ms up to a 5s deadline before any per-step check or capture (scripts/verify.mjs:59-77; scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:32-38; scripts/lib/inspect-checks.mjs:103-108). The unit tests do not drive a browser. repo-contract.test.ts:35-40 rejects playwright, chromium.launch and npm in tests/unit. The 200ms sleep in tests/unit/project-copy.test.ts:15 waits on a plain node child for the leak detector. The `waitForTimeout` in inspect-checks.test.ts:135 is a method on a fake page object. Judge A (pass) and Judge B (pass) match this reading. Judge C (fail) points to the fixed settle delays: SETTLE_MS in verify.mjs:63/78 and page.waitForTimeout(settleMs) in inspect-checks.mjs:108, plus the INT-002 `--settle-ms` timing test. That material does not decide the requirement. Those delays are in the delivered scripts under test, not in the tests. In each loop the settle runs only after `waitForIndex` has confirmed the step index, so it lets the entrance animation settle rather than standing in for a wait on step state. The review guidance says longer fixed settle delays neither earn credit nor fail a criterion. The INT-002 test at inspect.int.test.ts:62-68 asserts after the spawned process has exited and does not sleep itself.

verification-tooling.rationale: The review guidance says this criterion fails when the transition check turns a missing or non-numeric step hook into a number that still passes its comparison (example: Number(null) === 0 on the first step). In scripts/verify.mjs, read() guards against null but returns Number(value) for any other attribute value, so an empty or whitespace-only data-step-index becomes 0. waitForIndex then returns on `value === expected`, which accepts that 0 as first-step progress. This is the comparison failure the guidance names, so the 'pass' verdict is defeated.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs read(): `return value === null ? null : Number(value)`. Number('') and Number(' ') are both 0.
scripts/lib/checks.mjs waitForIndex: `if (value === expected) return`. The first call is waitForIndex(read, 0, ...), so a blank index hook satisfies it.

ci_claims.verbatim: ## Does "every pull request" in the test plan conflict with having no CI?
- **Requirement:** test-plan, execution lines for INT-001, INT-002, E2E-001, and E2E-002. CLAUDE.md says the repository has no hosted CI.

- **Ruling:** the merged check requires the `Appear` start delay to be at or above (`>=`) the layout transition's delay plus duration, and equality passes. The check fails only when a newcomer can start before persisting entities finish moving. An implementation that uses a strict `>` also passes.

- **Ruling:** confirmed. The kit supplies no visual defaults, and the check is not "no style attributes". Kit-owned inline style may hold only geometry and motion properties: position, size, offsets, transform, display/flex placement, overflow, z-index, pointer-events, and motion-driven opacity. It may not hold color, background, font, border, shadow, radius, margin, padding, gap, or any token. Caller `className`, `style`, and `data-*` props pass through, and the caller's style takes precedence. A component test renders with no caller props to check the allowlist, and again with caller props to check passthrough. The static scan covers CSS files, visual properties, and framework imports.

Product CI is explicitly absent for this revision: GitHub check-runs API returned `total_count: 0`, and no `.github` workflow files are present. The commit status list had one `CodeRabbit` success with description “Review skipped: draft pull request”; it is not product validation. The PR's sole comment is CodeRabbit's informational draft-review skip notice, not actionable implementation feedback. No current-head automated-validation evidence was supplied.
